name: GPT-OSS 120B
note: Groq free tier caps this model at 8000 TPM. Groq RESERVES max_tokens up front and refunds the unused part ~30s later, so a back-to-back 29-chair run drains the window and returns HTTP 413 'Request too large'. Run it one chair at a time with ~20s between calls (node bench/run.mjs --models groq-gptoss120b --only <chair-id>, which merges into the stored result).

name: your local model
baseUrlNote: Omitted on purpose: with no baseUrl the runner follows your OLLAMA_HOST (or OLLAMA_HOST_URL), which is the variable Ollama itself uses. Pin one here only if your server is somewhere those do not point.
numCtxNote: BENCHMARK SETTING ONLY. Capped so the bench measures the MODEL, not an eager KV allocation: Ollama reserves the whole KV cache at load, linear in num_ctx, so context is paid for in offloaded layers. Measured on one 8 GB card from ollama's own server.log: Qwen3-Coder-30B at -c 8192 put 49/49 layers on the GPU with a 768 MiB KV; the same model at -c 262144 put 9/49 on the GPU with a 24576 MiB KV, and graph splits went 104 -> 582. For daily use run the model at the largest context you actually need and buy it back with OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0, which halves KV bytes. Do NOT touch OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: current Ollama already passes --flash-attn auto so setting it to 1 is a no-op, and setting it to 0 additionally drops num_batch 512 -> 256 on CUDA devices with <= 8 GiB, making it a pessimisation on exactly the cards that need help.

name: Huihui Qwythos 9B
numCtxNote: BENCHMARK SETTING ONLY. Capped so the bench measures the MODEL, not an eager KV allocation: at its declared 262144 context Qwen3-Coder occupied 43 GB and ran 86% on CPU. For daily use run the model at its maximum context and buy it back with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 — context is what makes a model useful and starving it is not a speedup.
